original_question: Let Kn be the restriction to L^2([s,+infinity)) of the projection onto the first n probabilistic Hermite functions, with kernel Kn(x, y) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x) phi_k(y). Can one find a differential operator commuting with Kn on L^2([s,+infinity)), and what are its eigenvectors? The operator need not be second order, but it should converge in a suitable rescaled sense to LTW,s.
target_in_paper: Yacine Barhoumi-Andréani, "Some open problems in Random Matrix Theory and Orthogonal Polynomials", §2 "A related problem", Question 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation very closely: it defines K_n as the restriction to L^2([s,+infinity)) of the projection onto the first n probabilistic Hermite functions, asks for a differential operator commuting with K_n, asks for its eigenvectors, and preserves the paper's caveat that the commuting operator need not be second order but should tend, after suitable edge rescaling, to the Tracy-Widom/Airy-side commuting operator discussed immediately before Question 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
missing_details: Quantify the parameters explicitly: fix n in N and s in R. The paper states the problem in short-question form, so these quantifiers are implicit rather than written out. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Identify K_n explicitly as the GUE kernel operator, namely the restriction to L^2([s,+infinity)) of the orthogonal projection in L^2(R) onto span{phi_0,...,phi_{n-1}}; this terminology and motivation appear immediately before Question 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Make explicit that the intended limiting regime is the soft-edge/"at the edge" rescaling under which K_n converges to the Airy kernel operator; the paper uses that rescaling as the reason Question 2 is the finite-n analogue of Question 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Do not use L_TW,s as unexplained notation unless you define it: in the paper, the limit object is introduced contextually as the self-adjoint Tracy-Widom differential operator on L^2([s,+infinity)) commuting with the Airy kernel, cited from Tracy-Widom [1, § IV-B, p. 165]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Do not add extra requirements absent from the paper, such as self-adjointness of the finite-n operator, a fixed differential order, or a prescribed closed-form basis of eigenvectors. The official question asks only for a commuting differential operator and its eigenvectors, with the sole extra remark that second order is not required. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

No algebraic data such as homogeneity, degree bounds, ambient field/ring, or nilpotency conditions belong to this problem; it is purely an operator-theoretic question on L^2 spaces. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
refined_question: Fix n in N and s in R. Let K_n be the GUE kernel operator on L^2([s,+infinity)) obtained by restricting the orthogonal projection in L^2(R) onto the span of the first n probabilistic Hermite functions {phi_0,...,phi_{n-1}}, so that K_n has kernel K_n(x,y)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x)phi_k(y). Does there exist a differential operator D_{n,s} acting on L^2([s,+infinity)) such that D_{n,s}K_n=K_nD_{n,s}? If so, describe its eigenvectors. The sought operator is not required to be of second order, but under the standard soft-edge rescaling that sends K_n to the Airy kernel operator it should converge, in an appropriate sense, to the Tracy-Widom differential operator for the Airy kernel from Question 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
justification: The draft is targeting Question 2, not any Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3-type statement: this paper's matching item is the Barhoumi-Andréani open problem labeled Question 2. The wording of your draft tracks that question almost verbatim, and the only nearby context needed to make it fully stand-alone comes from the paragraph immediately preceding Question 2 and from Question 1: K_n is the finite-n GUE kernel built from the first n probabilistic Hermite functions, its edge rescaling gives the Airy kernel, and the limiting operator is the Tracy-Widom differential operator commuting with the Airy kernel. The paper does not supply a proved equivalent reformulation of Question 2, so no paper-backed alternate formulation should be invented. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
